title.en: What does a good life mean?

text.en: Ask a landless labourer, a rich farmer and a college student what development means and you will get three different answers. This chapter shows why, and how we compare countries.

Different people have different developmental goals. What is development for one may be unfair for another, and people often seek income, security, respect and freedom together.
A common measure is average income, also called per capita income, which is the total income of a country divided by its total population.
Income alone is not enough. Public facilities like health, education and a public distribution system also matter, and the Human Development Report of UNDP compares countries using health, education and income.
Kerala has a low infant mortality rate and high literacy, though its per capita income is lower than that of states such as Haryana. So higher income does not always mean better human development.
The Human Development Index combines life expectancy, years of schooling and income per person to rank countries.
Sustainability of development is also important. Resources like groundwater and fossil fuels are limited, so development must not harm future generations.
Averages can hide inequality. Two countries with the same average income may differ in how income is shared.
So development is a mix of income, public goods, equality and sustainability, not only money.

problem.en: Country A has total income Rs 6,00,000 and 3,000 people. What is its per capita income?

text.en: Per capita income = total income / population.

prompt.en: Explain why income alone does not measure development.

requiredIdeas.en: People want security, respect and health

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the richest country is the most developed

points.en: Per capita income is average income.
HDI uses health, education and income.
